title: E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022
currency: In force. Later amendments, if any, are not in the library.

scope.applies_to: Every manufacturer, producer, refurbisher, dismantler and recycler of e-waste or electrical and electronic equipment in Schedule I, including components, consumables, parts and spares.
excludes: waste batteries under the Battery Waste Management Rules, 2022
packaging plastics under the Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016

definitions.text: Electrical and electronic equipment, including solar photo-voltaic modules or panels or cells, whole or in part discarded as waste, as well as rejects from manufacturing, refurbishment and repair processes.
Any entity which has used at least one thousand units of electrical and electronic equipment listed in Schedule I at any point of time in the particular financial year, and includes e-retailer.
Non-branded or assembled electrical and electronic equipment, or those produced by a company which has closed its operations.

duties.text: Hand over e-waste only to a registered producer, refurbisher or recycler.

(1) Where e-waste is found mixed with municipal solid waste, segregate, collect and channelise it to a registered recycler or refurbisher; (2) collect and channelise orphan product e-waste; (3) facilitate e-waste collection, segregation and disposal systems; (4) conduct training to build local body capacity.
E-waste may be stored for up to 180 days, extendable by CPCB to 365 days.

schedule_i_notes: Schedule I includes fluorescent and other mercury-containing lamps (CEEW5) and solar photovoltaic panels (CEEW14).

routing_implications.summary: E-waste is not one of the four SWM streams. Where it turns up in municipal waste, the ULB must separate it and send it to a registered recycler or refurbisher (Schedule V, item 3). SWM Rules 2026 r. 9(7)(ii) lets a registered MRF act as the deposition centre for this.
routing_implications.planning_note: Institutions and offices using 1,000 or more EEE units a year are e-waste bulk consumers (r. 3(1)(b)). This is a different test from the SWM bulk waste generator criteria.
